title: Adaptive execpath tailor for architecture and sequence-length hints
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: We observe variable latency and cost across heterogeneous GPU fleets for mixed-prefill and decode workloads. Current static kernel preferences lead to tail latency regressions for short bursts on A100s and inefficiencies for long-context requests on H100-like instances. Goal: Implement a lightweight, request-scoped execpath tailor that uses fast architecture fingerprinting and sequence-length priors to pick a kernel execution plan (prefill vs decode tradeoffs, attention implementation variant, tiling) with minimal overhead. Approach should be safe (no SLO regressions), incremental (feature flags + canary), and observable.
success_metrics: Reduce 95th-percentile latency for <64-token user requests by 15% on mixed load clusters
Reduce avg token compute cost for >1024-token requests by 8% via better kernel packing
No increase in error rate or memory OOMs post rollout (<=0.1% change)
Decision latency budget for kernel choice < 1.5ms per request
acceptance_criteria: Lightweight fingerprinting hook implemented in runtime that emits arch and seqlen priors
A probe-and-score policy that selects between at least three kernel variants (fast-prefill, balanced, memory-compact) per request
Canary rollout to 5% traffic with automatic rollback on latency or error regression
End-to-end telemetry dashboards (per-model, per-region) with cost/latency delta vs baseline
design_decisions: Use microbench fingerprint (single-call, cached per-worker) rather than full microbenchmark at startup to avoid slow cold starts
Incorporate recent-seqlen histogram (windowed 15m) and per-customer override for deterministic workloads
Score kernels using a weighted objective: alpha*latency_est + beta*cost_est + gamma*safety_margin; alpha tuned for latency-sensitive tiers
Fallback policy: if selected kernel fails with OOMs or high latency, immediate soft-fallback to balanced execution and emit incident metric
implementation_notes: Phase 1: runtime hook + lightweight fingerprint and seqlen-prior collector (2w)
Phase 2: scoring function + config for customer tier weights + unit tests (1w)
Phase 3: canary infra and dashboards + e2e tests with synthetic tracebench (1w)
Phase 4: gradual rollout and postmortem/runbook update (1w)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: fingerprint overhead increases per-request latency; Mitigation: cache fingerprint per-worker and limit decision path to <1.5ms
Risk: misclassification for adversarial or highly variable seqlen workloads; Mitigation: add hysteresis and prefer safer kernel if uncertainty high
Risk: regression on rarer hardware combos; Mitigation: restrict early canary to specific regions and run offline synth benchmarks across fleet
